mainTopic: Which חטאת blood requires washing of a garment, the rules for dipping and sprinkling the blood, and what kinds of items need washing
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's rule that only חטאת blood received in a כלי and fit for sprinkling requires washing (כיבוס) of a garment it splashes on. The גמרא explains that this line gives the reason for the case of blood spilled on the floor. It also explains that 'fit for sprinkling' excludes small amounts caught in two כלים, each holding less than one sprinkling. רבי חלפתא בר שאול taught that rule about מי חטאת. The גמרא asks whether it also applies to blood, and רבי אלעזר rules that it does. רבא brings a ברייתא that reads וְטָבַל, בַּדָּם and מִן הַדָּם in the פסוק: the כהן must truly dip, a full amount must be in the כלי from the start, and the leftover blood on his finger is unfit. רבא defends that last rule against challenges from רבין בר רב אדא and אביי, and אביי explains that the finger is wiped on the rim of the bowl. A new משנה then argues whether a hide splashed with חטאת blood needs washing (רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר). It also says the washing and the cleaning of pots must be done in a holy place. The גמרא starts bringing the פסוק sources for each view, and רבי אלעזר's reading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need this extra line?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה adds the general rule about blood received in a כלי and fit for sprinkling, since it already taught that blood spilled on the floor does not require כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this line too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for seeming to repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said that if blood spilled on the floor and was gathered up, a garment it splashes on does not need washing. The general line 'only blood received in a כלי' seems to teach the same thing again. Since a משנה does not waste words, the גמרא asks what this line adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking why a line is not extra)

phrases.english: Why do I also need this?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's closing line: only blood received in a כלי and fit for sprinkling requires washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion on the משנה's closing line
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's general line 'אין טעון כיבוס אלא דם שנתקבל בכלי וראוי להזאה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case of blood spilled on the floor already teaches this, so the general line seems to repeat it.

steps.title: The line explains the reason for the earlier case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the line is not a new law. It explains why blood spilled on the floor and gathered up does not require כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is saying 'what is the reason.' Why does blood that spilled on the floor and was gathered up not require washing? Because only blood that was received in a כלי and is fit for sprinkling requires washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's line gives the reason for the earlier case. It is not a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is read as an explanation of the case before it. Blood that spilled on the floor was never received in a כלי, so it is not the kind of blood that requires כיבוס. Because the line works as an explanation, it is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It is saying 'what is the reason' (the line explains the earlier case)
Washing a garment that חטאת blood splashed on

phrases.english: It is saying, 'What is the reason?'
What is the reason that if it spilled on the floor
and he gathered it up, it does not require washing?
Because nothing requires washing
except blood that was received in a vessel
and is fit for sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the line is an explanation, not a separate law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to repeat the case of blood spilled on the floor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line gives the reason for that case, so it is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's line 'only blood received in a כלי and fit for sprinkling' gives the reason for the case of blood spilled on the floor.

steps.title: What does 'fit for sprinkling' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the words 'fit for sprinkling' come to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Fit for sprinkling': what does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses on the words 'fit for sprinkling' and asks what case they leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'received in a כלי' explain the case of blood on the floor. The גמרא assumes the extra words 'fit for sprinkling' must teach something more, and asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what? (what case do these words leave out)

phrases.english: 'Fit for sprinkling':
to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the line as a whole to one phrase inside it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the words 'ראוי להזאה' leave out

steps.title: It excludes small amounts in two separate vessels
steps.stepSummary: The words exclude a case where less than enough for one sprinkling was received in each of two כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes a case where he received less than enough for sprinkling in this כלי and less than enough for sprinkling in that כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'fit for sprinkling' leaves out blood split between two כלים, with neither holding enough for one sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each כלי on its own never held enough blood to sprinkle. So even if the blood is later combined, it does not count as blood that was received in a fit way. A garment it splashes on does not require כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the amount needed for one sprinkling
He received (the blood into a כלי)

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעוֹטֵי קִיבֵּל פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי הַזָּיָיה בִּכְלִי זֶה
phrases.english: To exclude where he received less than enough for sprinkling in this vessel
and less than enough for sprinkling in that vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ראוי להזאה' excludes blood received in two כלים, each holding less than the amount needed for one sprinkling.
steps.confusionAlert: The total blood may be enough for a sprinkling. What matters is that no single כלי ever held enough when the blood was received.

steps.title: Support from רבי חלפתא בר שאול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי חלפתא בר שאול: small amounts put in two separate כלים are not considered sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי חלפתא בר שאול says, if he sanctified less than enough for sprinkling in this כלי and less than enough for sprinkling in that כלי, he has not sanctified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the idea in step 4 comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חלפתא בר שאול rules that if each of two כלים held too little for one sprinkling, nothing became sanctified. The same idea, that each כלי must hold a full sprinkling's amount, supports the answer about blood.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲלַפְתָּא בַּר שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Ḥalafta bar Shaul says:

phrases.aramaic: קִידֵּשׁ פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי הַזָּיָיה בִּכְלִי זֶה
phrases.english: If he sanctified less than enough for sprinkling in this vessel
phrases.notes: This is about מי חטאת, the sprinkling water of purification, not about blood.

phrases.english: and less than enough for sprinkling in that vessel,
he has not sanctified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי חֲלַפְתָּא בַּר שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the answer in step 4
steps.raayaObject: The idea that amounts split between two כלים, each less than one sprinkling, do not count
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי חלפתא בר שאול about מי חטאת
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is about water, not blood. That gap sets up the question in the next step.

steps.title: Does the same rule apply to blood?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether רבי חלפתא's ruling also applies to blood. The first side is that it may be a special הלכה, and we do not learn other cases from such a הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law for blood? Is it a הלכה, and we do not learn from a הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question: does רבי חלפתא's ruling about water also apply to blood? It begins to lay out the first side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי חלפתא's ruling is a הלכה למשה מסיני, it stays limited to its own case, מי חטאת. Then it would not tell us anything about blood. The other side of the question comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
A הלכה (here meaning a law handed down from סיני)
We do not learn (other cases from it)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
With blood, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means blood received in two כלים, each with less than enough for one sprinkling.

phrases.english: Is it a halakha,
phrases.notes: He means a הלכה למשה מסיני, a law handed down orally from סיני.

phrases.english: and from a halakha we do not learn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the water ruling in step 5 also applies to blood
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי חלפתא's rule for מי חטאת also applies to חטאת blood, or whether it is a הלכה that stays limited to its own case
steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first side of the question, not a conclusion. The other side comes next.

steps.title: The other side: maybe the rule comes from a פסוק that also applies to blood
steps.stepSummary: The second side of the question: perhaps רבי חלפתא's rule comes from the words "וְטָבַל בַּמַּיִם", and the Torah says "וְטָבַל בַּדָּם" about blood too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the reason there (with the water) is that it is written "and dip in the water", and here too (with blood) it is written "and dip in the blood".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question from step 6. Maybe רבי חלפתא's rule is not a special הלכה but comes from a פסוק, and a matching פסוק exists for blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side said: if the rule is a הלכה with no source, we can't stretch it to blood. This side says: if the rule comes from the word "וְטָבַל", the same word appears with blood, so blood should follow the same rule. The next step settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: brings in the second side of a question

phrases.english: Or perhaps, there, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: "There" means רבי חלפתא's case of the water of purification from step 5.

phrases.english: Because it is written: "And dip it in the water";
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:18

phrases.english: here too it is written: "And dip in the blood."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in step 6 by giving its second option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי חלפתא's rule a special הלכה limited to water, or is it based on "וְטָבַל", which also appears with blood?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: blood is also not sanctified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's ruling that the same rule applies to blood: small amounts joined together are not sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: even with blood, it is not sanctified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from steps 6–7. רבי אלעזר says plainly that blood follows the same rule as the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two too-small amounts of blood were caught in separate כלים and then joined, the blood is not sanctified for sprinkling. This supports the second side: the rule is not limited to water.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the blood is not sanctified, blood like this that spills on a garment does not require כיבוס.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Even with blood, he did not sanctify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 6–7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי חלפתא's rule applies to blood too: combined small amounts of blood are not sanctified.

steps.title: רבא's ברייתא: reading each word of the פסוק about dipping in blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא that learns three rules from "וְטָבַל", "בַּדָּם" and "מִן הַדָּם", including that a full dipping amount must be in the כלי from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is taught in a ברייתא: "And he shall dip": and not wipe. "In the blood": there must be a dipping amount in the blood from the start. "Of the blood": from the blood spoken about in this topic.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא showing that the Torah's words about dipping in blood require a full amount of blood from the beginning. This backs up רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וְטָבַל" means the כהן must really dip, not wipe up a thin layer of blood. "בַּדָּם" means the full dipping amount must be there from the start, so adding blood later does not help. "מִן הַדָּם" means he sprinkles from that same blood in the כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: That is spoken about in this topic

phrases.english: Rava said: it is taught in a baraita:
"And he shall dip": and not wipe.
phrases.notes: There must be enough blood to dip into. He can't just wipe a little off the sides or bottom of the כלי with his finger.

phrases.english: "In the blood": unless there is in the blood
a measure for dipping from the start.
"Of the blood": of the blood that is in the topic.
phrases.notes: He means the blood already in the כלי, which the פסוק is talking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא source showing that blood needs a full amount from the start, in line with רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That blood for sprinkling must have a full dipping amount in the כלי from the beginning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading "וְטָבַל", "בַּדָּם" and "מִן הַדָּם" in ויקרא 4:6.

steps.title: Why the Torah needed the word "בַּדָּם"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that "וְטָבַל" alone would only require enough blood at the moment of dipping, so "בַּדָּם" was needed to require it from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was necessary to write "in the blood". If the Torah had written only "and he shall dip", I would have said it is fine even if there was no dipping amount from the start. So the Torah wrote "in the blood".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both words in the ברייתא are needed. Without "בַּדָּם" we would have learned the wrong rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From "וְטָבַל" alone we would only know there must be enough blood to dip when the כהן dips, even if it was added later. "בַּדָּם" adds a stricter rule: the full amount must be in the כלי from the very beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

steps.confusionAlert: "וְטָבַל" and "בַּדָּם" teach two different rules. "וְטָבַל" means enough to dip, not wipe. "בַּדָּם" means that amount must be there from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: Blood of a חטאת needs a full dipping amount in one כלי from the very beginning. Joining small amounts later does not sanctify it, just like רבי חלפתא's water.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "in the blood";
for if the Merciful One had written only "and he shall dip",
I would have said: even though
there was no measure for dipping from the start, it is fine;
so the Merciful One wrote "in the blood".
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets, "the Merciful One", and some don't. The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא needed both "וְטָבַל" and "בַּדָּם".
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity explanation (צריכותא): each word teaches something the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only "וְטָבַל", enough blood at the moment of dipping would be good enough, even if it was not there from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: "בַּדָּם" teaches that the full dipping amount must be in the כלי from the beginning.

steps.title: Why ״וְטָבַל״ is still needed after ״בַּדָּם״
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had only written ״בַּדָּם״, we might allow wiping blood from the walls of the כלי. So the Torah also wrote ״וְטָבַל״, which requires a real dipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only "in the blood," I would have thought that even wiping blood onto the finger is fine. So the Torah wrote "and he shall dip."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the other half of its answer. It already showed why ״בַּדָּם״ is needed, and now it shows why ״וְטָבַל״ is needed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בַּדָּם״ alone would only require enough blood in the כלי at the start. Later the כהן might just wipe the leftover blood off the walls of the כלי. ״וְטָבַל״ teaches that every sprinkling needs enough blood left to actually dip into.

keyTerms.meaning: And if [the Torah] had written (opens the second half of a צריכותא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the rule that each word in the פסוק adds a separate requirement, so neither word is extra.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "in the blood,"
I would have said that even if he wipes, it is fine;
phrases.notes: Wiping here means scraping the leftover blood off the walls of the כלי onto his finger, without a real dip.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote "and he shall dip."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in step 10, which explained why ״בַּדָּם״ was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word teaches something the other word could not teach alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only ״בַּדָּם״, wiping blood from the כלי's walls would be enough for later sprinklings.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְטָבַל״ requires enough blood to dip into for every sprinkling.

steps.title: What does ״מִן הַדָּם״ exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means to leave out when it says the blood must come ״מִן הַדָּם״, the blood being discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Of the blood" that is being discussed: what does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the third word in the ברייתא, ״מִן הַדָּם״, and asks what kind of blood it shuts out. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the sprinkling must be from the blood being discussed, meaning the blood in the כלי. The גמרא wants to know which other blood this rules out.

keyTerms.meaning: That is in the matter being discussed

phrases.english: "Of the blood": the blood that is in this matter,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:6. "In this matter" means the blood the פסוק is talking about, the blood in the כלי.

phrases.english: to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first two words of the ברייתא to its third derivation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which blood is excluded by the words ״מִן הַדָּם״.

steps.title: רבא: it excludes the leftover blood on the finger
steps.stepSummary: רבא says ״מִן הַדָּם״ excludes the blood left on the כהן's finger after a sprinkling. He must dip again for each sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It comes to exclude the leftover blood on the finger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The blood still on the finger after one sprinkling cannot be used for the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the כהן sprinkles, some blood stays on his finger. Since the פסוק says the blood must come from the blood in the כלי, this leftover blood does not count. He must dip again.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It comes to exclude the leftover blood that is on the finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״מִן הַדָּם״ excludes the leftover blood on the finger, which cannot be used for another sprinkling.

steps.title: This supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that this ברייתא backs up רבי אלעזר, who ruled that the leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אלעזר, since רבי אלעזר said: The leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that the ברייתא gives support to an earlier ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ruled that the blood left on the finger is unfit. The ברייתא's reading of ״מִן הַדָּם״ teaches the same thing, so it works as a proof for him.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
The leftover blood on the finger is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבא's answer to רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of ״מִן הַדָּם״, as explained by רבא.

steps.title: A ברייתא about blood spraying onto a garment
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא tells רבא that רב עמרם quoted a ברייתא: if blood sprays from the כהן's hand before he sprinkled, the garment must be washed, but after he sprinkled, it need not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said to רבא: Your student said that רב עמרם said: We learned: If he was sprinkling and some blood sprayed from his hand, before he sprinkled, the garment must be washed. Once he sprinkled, it does not need washing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין בר רב אדא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רבי אלעזר. Here he only quotes it, and the next step explains how it causes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of a חטאת that lands on a garment must be washed off only if the blood is still fit. The ברייתא splits the case into before and after he sprinkled. The question is what "before he sprinkled" covers.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרַב:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said to Rav:
phrases.notes: Here "רב" means רבא, the one who just made the statement about רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Your student said, Rav Amram said:
We have already learned:
If he was sprinkling and a sprinkle sprayed from his hand onto a garment,
if before he sprinkled, it requires washing.
phrases.notes: Fit חטאת blood on a garment must be washed out (ויקרא 6:20). So washing shows the blood was still fit.

phrases.english: If once he sprinkled, it does not require washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרַב: אָמַר תַּלְמִידְךָ, אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to go against the support for רבי אלעזר in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling, and רבא's support for it, that the leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about washing garments may show that blood on the finger is still fit until all the sprinklings are done.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as before the sprinklings are finished
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא explains the ברייתא this way: until all the sprinklings are finished, sprayed blood needs washing. That would mean the leftover blood on the finger is still fit, against רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא saying this: Before he finished sprinkling, the garment must be washed. Once he finished sprinkling, it does not need washing?
steps.whatsHappening: Here the challenge comes into focus. רבין בר רב אדא reads "before he sprinkled" as "before he finished all the sprinklings."
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, blood that sprays from the finger in the middle of the sprinklings still needs washing. That includes leftover blood on the finger. If it needs washing it must be fit, and that goes against רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so that...?, a suggested reading

phrases.english: What, is it not saying this:
before he finished sprinkling,
it requires washing,
once he finished sprinkling,
it does not require washing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא in step 15 challenges רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that the leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If blood sprayed before all the sprinklings are done needs washing, then the leftover blood on the finger is still fit.

steps.title: No: it means before the sprinkle left his hand
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא means before or after each single sprinkle leaves his hand. Blood left on the finger after a sprinkle does not need washing, so רבי אלעזר stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. This is what it says: Before the sprinkle left his hand, the garment must be washed. Once the sprinkle left his hand, it does not need washing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Before he sprinkled" refers to each single sprinkle, not the whole set. Blood that sprays before that sprinkle leaves his hand is fit and needs washing. The leftover on the finger after the sprinkle is unfit and needs no washing, just as רבי אלעזר said.
steps.whatToRemember: The leftover blood on the finger after a sprinkle is unfit (רבי אלעזר). The ברייתא about washing garments is about each single sprinkle, so it does not go against him.
steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the word "before." The whole argument is about what it means: before all the sprinklings are done, or before this one sprinkle leaves his hand.

phrases.english: No; this is what it is saying:
before the sprinkle left his hand,
it requires washing,
once the sprinkle left his hand,
it does not require washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; הָכִי קָאָמַר: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָצְתָה הַזָּאָה מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of step 16 and gives a different reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the ברייתא refers to each single sprinkle, not the end of all the sprinklings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Before he sprinkled" means before all the sprinklings are done, so the leftover on the finger is fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Before he sprinkled" means before this sprinkle leaves his hand, so the leftover on the finger is unfit, as רבי אלעזר said.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from the red heifer sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: when the כהן finishes sprinkling the פרה אדומה blood, he wipes his hand on the פרה. This suggests that he does not wipe in between sprinklings, so the leftover blood on his finger must be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged: The משנה says that when he finishes sprinkling, he wipes his hand on the body of the פרה. So only if he finished does he wipe. If he has not finished, he does not wipe!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה about the פרה אדומה to attack רבי אלעזר's rule that leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions wiping only at the end. אביי infers that between sprinklings the כהן does not wipe, so he keeps sprinkling with the blood left on his finger. That would make the leftover blood fit, which goes against רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה, the red heifer
If he finished, yes; if not, no (an inference from what the source says)

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
When he has finished sprinkling, he wipes his hand
on the body of the heifer.
If he finished, yes; if he has not finished, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא defended רבי אלעזר against רבין בר רב אדא, אביי brings a new challenge from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's rule that the leftover blood on the finger is unfit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions wiping only at the end. That implies no wiping between sprinklings, so leftover finger blood is used and must be fit.

steps.title: Wiping the hand at the end, wiping the finger in between
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה is talking about wiping the whole hand. At the end he wipes his whole hand on the פרה. In between sprinklings he wipes only his finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he finished, he wipes his hand on the body of the פרה. If he has not finished, he wipes his finger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rereads the משנה so that it no longer goes against רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'no wiping before he finishes' only means he does not wipe his whole hand on the פרה. He still wipes his finger after every sprinkling, so the leftover blood is never used. רבי אלעזר's rule stands.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: The one answering אביי here is רבא.

phrases.english: If he finished, he wipes his hand
on the body of the heifer;
if he has not finished, he wipes his finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the 'no' is about wiping the whole hand, not the finger
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Before he finishes, he does not wipe at all, so the leftover blood is fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before he finishes, he wipes only his finger, so the leftover blood is never used and רבי אלעזר stands.
steps.whatToRemember: After each sprinkling the finger is wiped. At the end the whole hand is wiped on the פרה. So the leftover blood is never used, just as רבי אלעזר said.

steps.title: Where does he wipe his finger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that at the end he wipes his hand on the פרה, because the פסוק says the פרה is burned with its blood. But between sprinklings, what does he wipe his finger on?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that when he finishes he wipes his hand on the body of the פרה, as the פסוק says, 'And the heifer shall be burned in his sight.' But his finger, what does he wipe it on?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up question about רבא's answer. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wiping at the end on the פרה has a reason: the leftover blood belongs with the פרה, which is burned with its blood. Between sprinklings there is no clear place to wipe the finger, so the גמרא asks where.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the heifer shall be burned in his sight'

phrases.english: Granted, if he finished, he wipes his hand
on the body of the heifer,
as it is stated: "And the heifer shall be burned in his sight."
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:5. The פסוק goes on to list the blood among what gets burned.

phrases.english: But his finger, on what does he wipe it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא גָּמַר מְקַנֵּחַ יָדוֹ בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about the finger-wiping that רבא described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the כהן wipes his finger on between sprinklings.

steps.title: He wipes his finger on the rim of the bowl
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the כהן wipes his finger on the rim of the bowl (מזרק). He brings support from the פסוק 'כפורי זהב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: On the rim of the bowl, as it is written, 'כפורי זהב', golden bowls.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question: the finger is wiped on the edge of the bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כפורי, used for bowls, is connected to the idea of wiping. This shows that bowls were used for wiping the finger. So רבא's reading of the משנה works in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Golden bowls' (the word כפורי is linked to wiping)

phrases.english: Abaye said: On the rim of the bowl,
as it is written: "Golden bowls [keforei]."
phrases.notes: עזרא 1:10. The word כפורי is understood as 'wiping,' so these are bowls you wipe your finger on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He wipes his finger on the rim of the bowl, supported by 'כפורי זהב'.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the discussion. The finger is wiped on the bowl's rim between sprinklings, so leftover finger blood is never sprinkled. רבי אלעזר's rule holds.

steps.title: New משנה: blood sprayed on an animal's hide
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. According to רבי יהודה, if חטאת blood sprays on a hide while it is still on the animal, it needs no washing. Once the hide has been skinned off, it needs washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If blood sprayed on the hide before it was skinned off, it does not need washing. After it was skinned off, it needs washing. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It asks which things that חטאת blood sprays on need כיבוס (washing).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hide still attached to the animal is part of the animal, not an item like a garment, so it needs no washing. Once it is skinned off, רבי יהודה treats it as an item that needs washing.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: נִיתַּז עַל הָעוֹר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הוּפְשַׁט –
phrases.english: If it sprayed onto the hide before it was skinned off,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the blood of a חטאת.

phrases.english: it does not require washing;
after it was skinned off, it requires washing.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on what kinds of things need washing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a hide still on the animal needs no washing. A hide that has been skinned off needs washing.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even a skinned hide needs no washing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי יהודה. Even after skinning, the hide needs no washing. Only the spot of the blood is washed, and only on an item that can become טמא and can be washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Even after it was skinned off, it does not need washing. Washing applies only to the spot of the blood, and only to an item that can become טמא and is fit for washing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the opposing view in the משנה and sets out the general rule for כיבוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, a plain skinned hide is not yet an item that can become טמא, so it needs no washing. He sets three conditions. You wash only the spot where the blood landed. The item must be able to become טמא. And it must be something that can be washed.

keyTerms.meaning: The spot where the blood landed

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי אלעזר in the משנה is a תנא. He is not the same person as the אמורא רבי אלעזר from earlier in the sugya, who ruled that the leftover blood on the finger is unfit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: Even after it was skinned off,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס אֶלָּא מְקוֹם הַדָּם,
phrases.english: it does not require washing. Washing is required only for the spot of the blood,
phrases.notes: The opening words, 'it does not require washing,' finish רבי אלעזר's ruling about the skinned hide. Then he starts his general rule.

phrases.english: and only on an item that is able to become impure,
and is fit for washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a skinned hide needs no washing. Washing applies only to the blood spot, on an item that can become טמא and can be washed.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three conditions are the basic rules for any חטאת blood that sprays onto something, and the גמרא will study each of them.

steps.title: Garment, sackcloth and hide all need washing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three kinds of material that need washing when חטאת blood sprays on them: a garment, sackcloth and a hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether it is a garment, sackcloth or a hide, all of them need washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and lists the kinds of material that must be washed when חטאת blood lands on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'garment' (בגד). The משנה widens this to sackcloth and hide too. This fits the rule just given in Step 23: the item must be able to become טמא and be washable.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment or piece of cloth
Sackcloth, a rough cloth woven from goat hair

phrases.english: Both the garment and the sackcloth
and the hide – all require washing;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד הַבֶּגֶד וְאֶחָד הַשַּׂק וְאֶחָד הָעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about washing off חטאת blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment, sackcloth and a hide that have חטאת blood on them all require washing.

steps.title: The washing and cleaning must be done in a holy place
steps.stepSummary: The washing, the breaking of a clay pot, and the scouring and rinsing of a copper pot all must be done in a holy place. This is a stringency of חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The washing must be done in a holy place. Breaking a clay pot must be done in a holy place. Scouring and rinsing a copper pot must be done in a holy place. This is a stringency that חטאת has more than the other most holy offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says where all this cleaning must happen: in a holy place, the עזרה. It ends by calling this an extra stringency of חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three acts are listed: washing cloth, breaking a clay pot, and cleaning a copper pot. All three must be done inside the holy area. Other קדשי קדשים do not have all of these rules, so this is something special about חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy place, meaning the עזרה (Temple courtyard)

steps.whatToRemember: With חטאת, washing the cloth, breaking the clay pot and scouring the copper pot are all done in a holy place. The משנה calls this a stringency of חטאת.

phrases.english: And the washing is in a holy place,
and the breaking of an earthenware vessel is in a holy place,
phrases.notes: This is the clay pot a חטאת was cooked in. The פסוק says that pot must be broken.

phrases.english: and scouring and rinsing of a copper vessel
is in a holy place.
This is a stringency of a sin offering beyond the other most holy offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds where the washing and cleaning must take place, and closes the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing, breaking a clay pot, and scouring and rinsing a copper pot used for חטאת are all done in a holy place. This is a stringency of חטאת.

steps.title: Where do these rules come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the argument in the משנה about a skinned hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source behind the argument of רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two opinions about a hide with blood on it (Steps 22-23). Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק each opinion is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: 'These matters' means the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר about the skinned hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה just completed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: A skinned hide is included from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns that a skinned hide also needs washing, from the words 'that on which it is sprinkled you shall wash'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'Garment' – that only teaches me a garment. From where do I include a hide after it was skinned? The פסוק says: 'that on which it is sprinkled you shall wash.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows how the פסוק includes a skinned hide, not only a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'garment' on its own would mean only cloth. The extra words 'that on which it is sprinkled' widen the rule to other things the blood lands on, such as a skinned hide.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (this word only teaches this much)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"Garment" – I have only a garment;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

phrases.english: from where do I include a hide after it was skinned?
The verse says: "That on which it is sprinkled you shall wash."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'אשר יזה עליה תכבס' include a skinned hide in the washing rule.

steps.title: A hide still on the animal is left out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects including a hide that is still on the animal. Like a garment, only something that can become טמא needs washing. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Might I include a hide even before it was skinned? The פסוק says 'garment': just as a garment can become טמא, so too anything that can become טמא. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes away a possible mistake, that even a hide still on the animal needs washing. It uses the word 'garment' to set a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'garment' becomes the model. Only items that, like a garment, can become טמא need washing. A hide on a living or unskinned animal cannot become טמא, so it is left out. This is the source for רבי יהודה's ruling in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too (comparing to a model)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree the item must be able to become טמא. Their argument is about the skinned hide. רבי יהודה says it fits the rule and needs washing. רבי אלעזר says it does not need washing (Step 23).

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה עוֹר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הוּפְשַׁט?
phrases.english: One might think that I include a hide even before it was skinned?
The verse says "garment" –
just as a garment is fit to become impure,
so too anything fit to become impure.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה עוֹר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הוּפְשַׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the inclusion from Step 27 so it does not cover a hide still on the animal.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects stretching the inclusion to a hide that is still on the animal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such a hide cannot become טמא, so it does not match the model of a garment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the פסוק source for רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה that a hide needs washing only after it is skinned.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר begins his own reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר starts reading the same word 'garment' and asks how sackcloth is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: 'Garment' – that only teaches me a garment. From where do I include sackcloth...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings רבי אלעזר's reading of the same פסוק. This line only sets up his reading, which continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר also starts from the word 'garment'. But the first thing he includes is sackcloth, not a skinned hide. That hints that he will use the פסוק differently from רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
"Garment" – I have only a garment;
from where do I include sackcloth

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יהודה's reading, the ברייתא turns to רבי אלעזר's reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר also reads 'garment' as only a starting point and goes on to include sackcloth.
